title: Human Rights Watch publishes Up in Flames on humanitarian law violations in the South Ossetia conflict
body:
On 23 January 2009 Human Rights Watch published Up in Flames, a 200-page report on humanitarian law violations in the conflict over South Ossetia, based on more than 460 interviews. A commentary by Tanya Lokshina on 30 January 2009 summarised its findings. The armed conflict lasted about one week in August 2008.

Human Rights Watch documented violations by all sides. It reported that South Ossetian forces killed several ethnic Georgian civilians, arbitrarily detained at least 159 ethnic Georgians, tortured at least four Georgian prisoners of war and executed at least three. It said Ossetian militias looted and burned homes on a wide scale in Georgian territory, sometimes with participation or passive acceptance by Russian forces, and that the conduct of Ossetian forces in several villages amounted to attempted ethnic cleansing.

On Georgian forces, Human Rights Watch reported indiscriminate and disproportionate artillery attacks, including extensive use of Grad multiple-rocket launchers in civilian areas, and use of cluster munitions. On Russian forces it reported indiscriminate aerial, artillery and tank fire that killed and wounded many civilians, cluster munitions use, and failure as an occupying power to ensure public order and safety. It said more than 20,000 ethnic Georgians remained displaced. In December 2008 94 governments signed a treaty banning cluster munitions; Russia and Georgia did not.
